intro: South Dakota runs its elections county by county, through each county auditor.

id_rule.text: Bring a photo ID: a South Dakota driver's license or ID card, a U.S. passport or other U.S. government photo ID, a U.S. Armed Forces ID, a tribal photo ID, or a current photo ID from a South Dakota high school or college. If you don't have one, you can sign a personal identification affidavit and still vote a regular ballot.

elections.name: General election
elections.what: Federal, state and local offices, plus any statewide or local measures. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: Absentee voting begins
dates.detail: You can vote absentee in person at your county auditor's office. To vote by mail, send your signed application to your county election official.

dates.label: Last day to register to vote
dates.detail: Your signed registration form must reach your county auditor 15 days before Election Day. South Dakota does not accept registration by fax or email.

src.label: SD Secretary of State - 2026 election information

dates.label: In-person absentee request deadline
dates.detail: In-person requests are taken until 5 pm on the day before the election. A person who is sick or disabled can use a messenger, and that request must arrive before 3 pm on Election Day.

src.label: SD Secretary of State - absentee voting

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Polls are open 7 am to 7 pm local time. A voted absentee ballot must reach your county election official on Election Day, in time to get to your precinct before the polls close.
